verses.1:1: Song of Songs, which belongs to Solomon.
verses.1:2: Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth, for your breasts are better than wine, and the fragrance of your perfumes is beyond all spices.
verses.1:3: Your name is perfume poured out. Therefore young women have loved you,
verses.1:4: they have drawn you; we will run after you, toward the fragrance of your perfumes. The king has brought me into his chamber. Let us exult and be glad in you; we will love your breasts more than wine; uprightness has loved you.
verses.1:5: I am black and beautiful, daughters of Israel, like the tents of Kedar, like the curtain of Solomon.
verses.1:6: Do not look at me because I am blackened, because the sun has looked sideways at me. The sons of my mother fought against me; they set me as a guard in vineyards; my own vineyard I did not guard.
verses.1:7: Tell me, you whom my soul has loved, where you pasture, where you rest at noon, so that I never become like one veiled beside the herds of your comrades.
verses.1:8: If you do not know yourself, beautiful one among women, go out yourself on the heels of the flocks, and pasture your young goats beside the tents of the shepherds.
verses.1:9: To my mare among the chariots of Pharaoh I have compared you, my companion.
verses.1:10: How lovely your cheeks have become like turtledoves, your neck like necklaces!
verses.1:11: We will make likenesses of gold for you with dots of silver.
verses.1:12: While the king was on his reclining couch, my nard gave forth its fragrance.
verses.1:13: A bundle of myrrh is my kinsman to me,
verses.1:15: Look, you are beautiful, my companion; look, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves.
verses.1:16: Look, you are handsome, my kinsman, and indeed lovely; moreover, our couch is shaded;
verses.1:17: the beams of our houses are cedars, our paneled ceilings are cypresses.
verses.2:1: I am a flower of the plain, a lily of the valleys.
verses.2:2: Like a lily in the midst of thorns, so is my companion among the daughters.
verses.2:3: Like an apple tree among the trees of the forest, so is my kinsman among the sons. In his shade I longed and sat down, and his fruit is sweet in my throat.
verses.2:4: Bring me into the house of wine; set love over me.
verses.2:5: Strengthen me with perfumes, cushion me with apples, for I am wounded by love.
verses.2:6: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
verses.2:7: I have put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you do not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
verses.2:8: The voice of my kinsman! Look, here he comes, leaping upon the mountains, bounding over the hills.
verses.2:9: My kinsman is like a gazelle or a fawn of stags upon the mountains of Bethel. Look, there he is behind our wall, peering through the windows, peeking through the lattices.
verses.2:10: My kinsman answers and says to me, "Rise up, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove.
verses.2:11: For look, the winter has passed; the rain has gone away, it has gone on its way;
verses.2:12: the flowers have appeared in the land, the time of pruning has arrived, the voice of the turtledove has been heard in our land;
verses.2:13: the fig tree has put forth its early figs; the vines are in blossom, they have given forth fragrance. Rise up, come, my companion, my beautiful one, my dove. And come,
verses.2:14: you, my dove, in the shelter of the rock, next to the outer wall, show me your appearance, and let me hear your voice, for your voice is sweet, and your appearance is lovely."
verses.2:15: Catch for us little foxes that ruin vineyards, and our vineyards are in blossom.
verses.2:16: My kinsman is mine, and I am his, the one who pastures among the lilies,
verses.2:17: until the day breathes and the shadows shift. Turn back; you, kinsman, be like a gazelle or a fawn of stags upon mountains of hollows.
verses.3:1: On my bed in the nights I sought him whom my soul has loved; I sought him, and I did not find him; I called him, and he did not answer me.
verses.3:2: I will rise up now and go around in the city, in the marketplaces and in the broad streets, and I will seek him whom my soul has loved. I sought him, and I did not find him.
verses.3:3: The watchmen found me, those who go around in the city: "Have you seen him whom my soul has loved?"
verses.3:4: It was just a little while after I passed from them before I found him whom my soul has loved; I took hold of him and did not let him go, until I brought him into the house of my mother and into the chamber of her who conceived me.
verses.3:5: I have put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you do not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
verses.3:6: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, scented with myrrh and frankincense, from all the powders of a perfumer?
verses.3:7: Look, the couch of Solomon: sixty mighty men are around it, from the mighty men of Israel,
verses.3:8: all holding a sword, trained in war; each man has his sword upon his thigh because of terror in the nights.
verses.3:9: King Solomon made for himself a palanquin from the timbers of Lebanon.
verses.3:10: He made its pillars of silver, and its backrest golden; its seat is purple, its interior is inlaid with stone, love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.3:11: Go out and look upon King Solomon, in the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding and on the day of the gladness of his heart.
verses.4:1: Look, you are beautiful, my companion; look, you are beautiful. Your eyes are doves, apart from your silence. Your hair is like flocks of goats that were revealed from Gilead.
verses.4:2: Your teeth are like flocks of the shorn ones that came up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and there is not a childless one among them.
verses.4:3: Like a scarlet cord are your lips, and your speech is lovely; like the rind of a pomegranate is your cheek, apart from your silence.
verses.4:4: Like the tower of David is your neck, built for Thalpioth; a thousand shields hang on it, all the javelins of the mighty ones.
verses.4:5: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, that graze among lilies.
verses.4:6: Until the day breathes and the shadows move, I will go for myself to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of Lebanon.
verses.4:7: You are entirely beautiful, my companion, and there is no blemish in you.
verses.4:8: Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon; you will come and pass through from the beginning of faith, from the peak of Senir and Hermon, from dens of lions, from mountains of leopards.
verses.4:9: You have heartened us, my sister, my bride; you have heartened us with one of your eyes, with one, with a necklace of your neck.
verses.4:10: How much more beautiful have your breasts become than wine, and the fragrance of your garments above all spices?
verses.4:11: Your lips drip honeycomb, bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon.
verses.4:12: A closed garden is my sister, my bride, a closed garden, a sealed spring.
verses.4:13: Your shoots are an orchard with fruit of choice trees, henna plants with spikenards;
verses.4:14: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon with all the trees of Lebanon, myrrh, aloes, with all the finest perfumes;
verses.4:15: a spring of a garden and a well of water, living and rushing from Lebanon.
verses.4:16: Awake, north wind; and come, south wind, and blow through my garden, and let my spices flow.
verses.5:1: Let my beloved come down into his garden and eat the fruit of his choice trees. I have entered into a garden, my sister, my bride; I have gathered my myrrh with my spices, I have eaten my bread with my honey, I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, and drink and become drunk, brothers.
verses.5:2: I am sleeping, and my heart is awake. The voice of my beloved! He is knocking at the door: "Open to me, my sister, my companion, my dove, my perfect one, for my head has been filled with dew and my locks with the drops of the night."
verses.5:3: I have taken off my tunic; how should I put it on? I have washed my feet; how will I soil them?
verses.5:4: My beloved sent his hand from the opening, and my belly was stirred for him.
verses.5:5: I rose to open to my beloved; my hands dripped myrrh, my fingers full myrrh, on the handles of the bolt.
verses.5:6: I opened to my beloved; my beloved had passed by; my soul went out at his word; I sought him and did not find him, I called him and he did not answer me.
verses.5:7: The watchmen who go around in the city found me; they struck me, they wounded me; the watchmen of the walls took my shawl from me.
verses.5:8: I have put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field: if you find my beloved, what should you report to him? That I am wounded with love.
verses.5:9: What is your beloved more than another beloved, beautiful one among women, what is your beloved more than another beloved, that you have put us under oath like this?
verses.5:10: My beloved is white and ruddy, selected out from ten thousands.
verses.5:11: His head is gold and phaz; his locks are palm shoots, black as a raven.
verses.5:12: His eyes are like doves beside full pools of water, washed in milk, sitting beside full pools.
verses.5:13: His cheeks are like bowls of spice producing aromatics; his lips are lilies dripping full myrrh.
verses.5:14: His hands are turned gold, filled with tarshish. His belly is an ivory tablet on a sapphire stone.
verses.5:15: His legs are marble pillars founded on golden bases; his appearance is like Lebanon, choice as cedars.
verses.5:16: His throat is sweetnesses, and he is wholly desire. This is my beloved, and this is my companion, daughters of Jerusalem.
verses.6:1: Where has your beloved gone, beautiful one among women? Where has your beloved looked? And we will seek him with you.
verses.6:2: My brother has gone down into his garden, to bowls of spice, to shepherd in gardens and to gather lilies.
verses.6:3: I belong to my beloved, and my beloved belongs to me, the one who shepherds among the lilies.
verses.6:4: You are beautiful, my companion, like good pleasure, lovely as Jerusalem, astonishment like those drawn up in array.
verses.6:5: Turn away your eyes from facing me, for they have set me aflutter. Your hair is like flocks of goats that appeared from Gilead,
verses.6:6: your teeth are like flocks of the shorn ones that came up from the washing, all of them bearing twins, and there is not a childless one among them. Like a scarlet cord are your lips, and your speech is lovely.
verses.6:7: Like the rind of a pomegranate is your cheek, apart from your silence.
verses.6:8: There are sixty queens, and eighty concubines, and young women of whom there is no number;
verses.6:9: one is my dove, my perfect one; she is the only one to her mother, she is choice to the one who bore her. Daughters saw her and will call her blessed, queens and even concubines, and they will praise her.
verses.6:10: Who is this who peers forth like the dawn, beautiful as the moon, choice as the sun, astonishment like those drawn up in array?
verses.6:11: Into a nut-tree garden I went down to look among the produce of the brook, to see whether the vine blossomed, the pomegranates bloomed forth; there I will give my breasts to you.
verses.6:12: My soul did not know; it made me the chariots of Amminadab.
verses.7:1: Return, return, Shunammite; return, return, and we will look on you. What will you see in the Shunammite? She who comes like dances of the camps.
verses.7:2: Your steps are beautiful in sandals, daughter of Nadab. The proportions of your thighs are like necklaces, the work of a craftsman.
verses.7:3: Your navel is a carved mixing bowl, not lacking mixed wine; your belly is a heap of wheat fenced in with lilies.
verses.7:4: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
verses.7:5: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like pools in Heshbon, at the gates of the daughter of many. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking out toward the face of Damascus.
verses.7:6: Your head upon you is like Carmel, and the braid of your head is like purple; a king is bound in galleries.
verses.7:7: How beautiful you are, and how sweet you are, love, in your delights!
verses.7:8: This is your stature: you are likened to the palm tree, and your breasts to the clusters.
verses.7:9: I said, "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its heights." And now your breasts will be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your nose like apples,
verses.7:10: and your throat like the good wine, going straight to my kinsman, sufficing for my lips and teeth.
verses.7:11: I belong to my kinsman, and his turning is toward me.
verses.7:12: Come, my kinsman, let us go out into the field; let us lodge in the villages.
verses.7:13: Let us go early to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has bloomed, the vine-blossom has bloomed, the pomegranates have bloomed; there I will give my breasts to you.
verses.7:14: The mandrakes have given off fragrance, and at our doors are all choice fruits; new alongside old, my kinsman, I have kept for you.
verses.8:1: Who would give you as my kinsman, nursing at the breasts of my mother? Finding you outside, I will kiss you, and indeed they will not despise me.
verses.8:2: I will take you, I will bring you into the house of my mother and into the chamber of her who conceived me; I will give you to drink from the spiced wine, from the juice of your pomegranates.
verses.8:3: His left hand is under my head, and his right hand will embrace me.
verses.8:4: I have put you under oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you do not rouse or awaken love until it wishes.
verses.8:5: Who is this coming up made white, leaning on her beloved? Under an apple tree I awakened you; there your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor with you.
verses.8:6: Place me like a seal upon your heart, like a seal upon your arm; for love is mighty like death, jealousy is harsh like Hades; its wings are wings of fire, its flames.
verses.8:7: Much water will not be able to quench love, and rivers will not flood over it. If a man gives all his livelihood for love, they will utterly despise him.
verses.8:8: We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day when she is spoken of?
verses.8:9: If she is a wall, let us build silver battlements upon her; and if she is a door, let us mark out a cedar board upon her.
verses.8:10: I am a wall, and my breasts are towers; I was in their eyes like one who finds peace.
verses.8:11: A vineyard belonged to Solomon in Beethlamon; he gave his vineyard to the keepers; each man will bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.
verses.8:12: My vineyard, my own, is before me; the thousand are for Solomon, and the two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
verses.8:13: You who sit in the gardens, companions are paying attention to your voice; let me hear it.
verses.8:14: Flee, my kinsman, and be like a gazelle or a fawn of the deer upon the mountains of spices.

notes.1:2: Greek reads "your breasts" (mastoi sou, also in 1:4), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonants from the Masoretic Text ("your love").
notes.1:5: This Greek text reads "daughters of Israel," whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text and some other Greek witnesses read "daughters of Jerusalem."
notes.1:8: Greek translates the Hebrew ethical dative literally as a reflexive object, "If you do not know yourself" (ean me gnos seauten), rather than simply "If you do not know."
notes.1:10: Greek reads "like turtledoves" (hos trygones), taking the Hebrew word torim in the sense of "turtledoves" rather than "ornaments" or "plaits."
notes.1:13: Greek adelphidos literally denotes a nephew or close male relative ("kinsman") and is used throughout the Septuagint Song of Songs for the male beloved (Hebrew dod). This Greek text also omits the clauses at the end of 1:13 and start of 1:14 found in the Hebrew MT and some Greek witnesses, likely due to scribal eye-skip across the repeated phrase "my kinsman to me."
notes.2:1: Greek renders the Hebrew geographic term Sharon as a common noun, "of the plain" (tou pediou), and reads "flower" (anthos) rather than "rose."
notes.2:4: Greek uses plural imperatives ("Bring me... set love over me") where the Hebrew MT has third-person narrative ("He brought me... his banner over me was love"), and in 2:5 reads "with perfumes" and "wounded" rather than "with raisin cakes" and "lovesick."
notes.2:7: Greek renders the Hebrew terms for gazelles and does as "powers" (dynamesin) and "strengths" (ischysesin, so also in 3:5). The conditional particle ean (literally "if") follows the Hebraic oath idiom functioning as a solemn prohibition ("that you do not").
notes.2:9: Greek includes the place-name "Bethel" ("upon the mountains of Bethel"), which is not in the Hebrew MT here; in 2:17 Greek translates Hebrew "mountains of Bether" as "mountains of hollows."
notes.2:12: Greek specifically renders the ambiguous Hebrew noun zamir as "pruning" (tes tomes) rather than "singing."
notes.3:1: Greek includes the final clause "I called him, and he did not answer me," which is absent from the Hebrew MT in 3:1 (compare 5:6).
notes.3:10: Greek renders Hebrew rasup ("inlaid/fitted") concretely as "inlaid with stone" (lithostroton), followed by the accusative "love" (agapen).
notes.3:11: This Greek text omits the vocative "daughters of Zion" found in the Hebrew MT and some other Greek witnesses.
notes.4:1: Greek ektos tes siopeseos sou literally reads "apart from your silence" (also in 4:3 and 6:7), reflecting the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew term for "veil," and apekalyphthesan literally means "were revealed" (contrast "appeared" in 6:5).
notes.4:4: Thalpioth is the Septuagint transliteration of an obscure Hebrew word often understood as "courses" or "armory," and Greek bolides specifically means "javelins" or "darts" rather than shields.
notes.4:8: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew mountain name Amana etymologically as pisteos ("faith"), yielding "from the beginning of faith."
notes.4:9: Greek ekardiosas hemas uses a rare verb coined from "heart" ("heartened") with a plural object ("us"), and the closing phrase literally reads "with one, with a necklace of your necks."
notes.4:10: Greek mastoi sou literally reads "your breasts" (compare 6:11), reflecting a different vocalization of the Hebrew consonantal text where the Masoretic Text reads "your love."
notes.5:1: Greek adelphidos (literally "nephew" or "dear kinsman") serves throughout Septuagint Song of Songs as a term of endearment ("beloved"). The Greek text here also reads "into a garden" (without "my"), "my bread" (where the Hebrew has "my honeycomb"), and "brothers" (where the Hebrew has "beloved/lovers").
notes.5:8: The Septuagint includes the oath formula "by the powers and by the strengths of the field" (absent from Hebrew 5:8, echoing 2:7 and 3:5) and reads tetromene agapes ("wounded with love") rather than "lovesick."
notes.5:11: Greek chrysion kai phaz ("gold and phaz") partially transliterates the Hebrew expression ketem paz ("pure gold").
notes.5:13: Greek phialai tou aromatos literally means "bowls of spice" (also in 6:2), and phyousai myrepsika ("producing aromatics") reflects a Hebrew participle read as "growing" rather than "towers."
notes.5:14: Greek tharseis ("tarshish") transliterates the Hebrew name of a precious stone (often identified as chrysolite or beryl), and the second clause literally places the ivory tablet "on a sapphire stone."
notes.6:2: Here the Greek text reads Adelphos mou ("My brother") rather than adelphidos mou ("my beloved"), which appears in 6:1 and 6:3.
notes.6:4: The Septuagint translates the Hebrew city name Tirzah etymologically as eudokia ("good pleasure"), and renders the closing phrase literally as "astonishment like those drawn up in array" (repeated in 6:10).
notes.6:6: The second sentence ("Like a scarlet cord are your lips, and your speech is lovely.") is present in the Septuagint here (matching 4:3), though absent from the Hebrew text.
notes.6:11: The closing clause "there I will give my breasts to you" is a Septuagint addition in this verse, echoing 7:13 (Eng. 7:12).
notes.6:12: This verse is difficult in both Hebrew and Greek; following the Greek punctuation and double accusative, "my soul" is the subject of "did not know," and Ameinadab (Amminadab) is rendered as a proper name.
notes.7:1: The Greek reads "Shunammite" (Σουμανεῖτις, the Septuagint form for the Shunammite in 1-2 Kings) rather than the Masoretic Text's "Shulammite," and introduces the response with "She who comes" (ἡ ἐρχομένη).
notes.7:2: The Greek takes Hebrew nadiv ("noble") as the proper name "Nadab" (Ναδάβ).
notes.7:5: The Greek translates the Hebrew place name Bath-rabbim literally as "daughter of many" (θυγατρὸς πολλῶν).
notes.7:10: Greek ἀδελφιδός (literally "nephew" or "kinsman") is used consistently throughout the Greek Song of Songs as the term of affection for the beloved (including in 8:1). The closing clause "sufficing for my lips and teeth" (ἱκανούμενος χείλεσίν μου καὶ ὀδοῦσιν) reflects a Greek reading distinct from the Masoretic Text ("gliding over the lips of sleepers").
notes.7:13: The Greek reads "my breasts" (τοὺς μαστούς μου) where the Masoretic Text reads "my love," differing only in Hebrew vocalization.
notes.8:2: The Greek reads "and into the chamber of her who conceived me" (matching 3:4, whereas the Masoretic Text has "she who would teach me") and "your pomegranates" (ῥοῶν σου) rather than "my pomegranates."
notes.8:4: Unlike the Masoretic Text in this verse, the Greek includes "by the powers and by the strengths of the field" (rendering Hebrew terms for gazelles and does as "powers" and "strengths"), and uses the Hebraic oath particle ἐάν (literally "if") to express a solemn prohibition.
notes.8:5: The Greek reads "made white" (λελευκαθισμένη, meaning completely white or clothed in white) where the Masoretic Text reads "from the wilderness."
notes.8:6: Greek περίπτερα literally means "wings" or "pinions" (rendering Hebrew "flashes"), and the verse ends simply with "its flames" (φλόγες αὐτῆς) without the Masoretic Text's divine element ("flame of Yah").
notes.8:11: The Greek text gives the place name "Beethlamon" (Βεεθλαμών), corresponding to "Baal-hamon" in the Masoretic Text.
